title: Sidestep deploy chronicle and thumbprint notes — Sept 2026 (wip)
body:
Context and goal:

This is a working notes doc for the Sidestep mini-release (feature flags + routing change) that we plan to shepherd through a compact 48-hour window. Purpose: provide an hour-by-hour operator slate, concise checklists for each lane (staging, canary, regionA/B), and a small draft of release notes for customers and internal comms. Not polished; use as the single source during the launch run.

Quick summary (one-liner):
- Ship stable routing fallback for user-assigned model variants; avoid cross-region cache thrash; maintain 95th percentile latency SLAs during spike.

Primary risks we care about:
- KV cache misalignment between model variants -> increased token latency
- Unexpected autoscale cold starts in region B (APAC) due to different traffic pattern
- Rollout causing 10–15% spike in edge traffic that could hit quota throttles

Ownership and on-call roster (48h):
- Release lead: Priya Desai (owner)
- Serving runtime: Ethan Park
- Traffic/Ingress: Lena Rodriguez
- SRE/Autoscale: Noah Kim
- Observability: Mei Tan (on-call observability)
- Customer comms: Jordan Mills

Channeling and alerts:
- Primary comms channel: #deploys-weekly (pinned messages include this doc link + Linear ticket)
- Pager/ops escalation: Pager duty runbook "Release Pagers -> Infra"

High-level cadence (local times are UTC):
- T-36h: Final smoke test run in staging (full prefix cache scenario)
- T-24h: Traffic shadowing enabled (10% shadow) in production routing for 3 hours
- T-6h: Canary window opens (0.5% traffic -> 2% -> 5% over 40m increments)
- T+2h: Full rollout to region A if canary stable; region B staggered + extra hold at 10%
- T+24h: Post-rollout sampling and regression evals; decide whether to flip feature flag to default

Hour-by-hour run slate (detailed):
- T-36h (48h before final rollback cutoff):
  - 09:00 UTC: Staging smoke (checklist below) — owner: Ethan
  - 10:30 UTC: Quick retro of integration tests, confirm no blocking PRs — owner: Priya
  - Deliverable: staging-smoke-OK in Linear (SID-122)

- T-24h:
  - 12:00 UTC: Shadow config applied (traffic router) 10% shadowing for 3 hours — owner: Lena
  - 12:05 UTC: Observability hooks enabled and sampling set to 100% for traces matching sidestep routing header — owner: Mei
  - 12:30 UTC: Checkpoint: latency baseline captured and saved (artifact id in linked_artifacts) — owner: Mei

- T-6h (pre-canary checks):
  - Inventory and capacity check: confirm dedicated pool free GPUs >= 12, burst slots >= 6 — owner: Noah
  - Helm diff + config-lite review (feature flags, rollout gates) — owner: Priya
  - Notify customer success for any high-touch customers in region B — owner: Jordan

- Canary window (T-0 -> T+2h):
  - 00:00 UTC: Open canary at 0.5% (route header=\"sidestep-canary\") — owner: Lena
  - 00:20 UTC: Observe 95th latency, error rate, cache hit ratio; if stable -> move to 2% — owner: Mei
  - 00:40 UTC: Repeat checks -> 5% over next 40 minutes if healthy
  - Abort criteria (immediate rollback):
    - 95th latency regresses >20% from baseline AND sustained for 5 minutes
    - Error rate increases >0.5 percentage points absolute
    - Cache hit ratio drops >10% leading to token cost spike
  - If abort criteria hit: run rollback cheat (see rollback section) and call incident channel

- Full rollout and region stagger (T+2h -> T+8h):
  - Route increase to 20% then 50% with 15m holds at each step for telemetry checks — owner: Lena
  - Region B: hold additional 30 minutes between 10% -> 30% bump — owner: Noah (watch autoscale metrics)
  - Reserve burst capacity in Dedicated: pre-warm 4 nodes for 30 minutes before region B bump

- Post-rollout (T+24h -> T+48h):
  - Sampling evals for quality regressions using eval set 'thumbprint-core-2026' — owner: Applied ML (Ethan lead)
  - Cost sampling: token unit cost for sidestep variant vs baseline across 8hr rolling window — owner: Priya
  - Final decision checkpoint on feature flag: flip to default or keep opt-in — owner: Priya + Product PM

Staging smoke checklist (T-36h):
- Deploy candidate artifact to staging cluster
- Load user prefixes from sample set (prefixes-5000) and run 1k synthetic sessions
- Validate KV cache hits >= 92% for warmed prefixes
- Validate sequence length tail handling for 4k tokens (p99 latency under 2.5s for staging GPU)
- End-to-end latencies measured and recorded in 'staging-smoke' notebook
- Create quick-fix playbook snippet if any test fails (link to Linear)

Operator quick commands (cheat sheet):
- Rollback (immediate): rinfctl rollout cancel sidestep && rinfctl route set default
- Drain step: kubectl cordon node-<id> && rinfctl drain-evict node-<id> (use for hotfix)
- Re-pin model: rinfctl model pin <customer-model> <baseline-tag>

Rollback matrix (decision ladder):
- Transient metric blip (<5m) -> hold and observe; do not rollback
- Sustained regression (>=5m meeting abort criteria) -> immediate rollback to previous stable routing config + notify customers
- Severe outage (customer-visible errors >3%) -> emergency rollback + open incident call and alert execs

Telemetry gating thresholds (operational):
- latency_95pct: baseline*1.20 -> alert
- error_rate_percent: baseline + 0.5 -> alert
- kv_cache_hit_ratio: baseline - 10% -> alert
- autoscale_cold_start_count: >3 in 10m window -> SRE investigate

Capacity reservation and quick table (plain text):
- Dedicated GPU pool: reserved 12 units (g4x.4 equiv) for 6 hours starting T-2h
- Burst nodes: 6 pre-warmable, 4 pinned for region B
- Traffic quota: confirm edge throttles allow +15% transient — contact infra-quotas if not

Release notes draft (customer-facing, short):
Title: Gradual rollout of per-customer routing fallback (Sidestep)
Summary: We are deploying a routing improvement that reduces cross-variant cache misses for user-specific models and improves latency consistency for long-context workloads. This is a gradual, monitored rollout. If you experience increased latency or errors that correlate with the header \"sidestep-route\", contact support and we can pin you back to the previous routing immediately.
Details and impact:
- Expected benefits: reduced variance in response latency for sessions over 1k tokens, fewer dropped tokens in edge cases, improved model variant isolation.
- Known limitations: During rollout there is a small chance of transient cache warmups; we will monitor and back out quickly if needed.
- Opt-out: Customer teams can request temporary pinning by opening a support ticket or emailing customer-success@redwood.ai

Internal release notes (for ops):
- Artifact: sidestep-release-2026-09-12 (sha: abc123def)
- Main config changes: updated router weighting, new header flag for canary, KV cache TTL bumped from 15m -> 20m for warm lanes
- Observability knobs changed: sampling for sidestep traces -> 100% during canary window

Unresolved open questions (to resolve before T-6h):
- Are there any enterprise customers scheduled for maintenance in region B that might confound telemetry? (Jordan to confirm)
- Should we apply a shorter KV TTL for cold starts in region B as a mitigation? (Noah to propose)

Post-mortem hooks (if we hit rollback):
- Immediate artifact: capture full traffic dump for 15 minutes prior to rollback
- Root-cause anchors: config diff, autoscale logs, KV eviction logs
- Timeline: write first-pass timeline within 6 hours and fill in detailed RCA within 48 hours

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Keep the canary header simple (\"sidestep-canary\") and documented in the router README
- Keep a separate quick-link in Slack for restart commands — avoid typing long rinfctl sequences in a hot incident
- If Mei sees trace sampling anomalies, increase trace TTL to capture more context before bumping traffic

Appendix: Short link artifacts and tickets referenced:
- Linear: SID-122 (primary), SID-121 (preflight), SID-130 (customer follow-ups)
- Confluence: Deploy-Playbook-Thumbprint-2026-09 (detailed runbook)
- Observability dashboard: obs.redwood.internal/dashboards/sidestep-canary

End of working doc — update as we progress through preflight and canary.

PRIYA
